tasks.title: Add LLM client (provider-neutral) + graceful fallback — Phase 5 foundation
tasks.notes: No LLM SDK installed — gates all of Phase 5 (t23 AI analyst, t24 natural-language Q&A). Recommended: MiniMax via openai pkg baseURL override.

prep.what: Install `openai` npm package and create `lib/ai/client.ts` — a small provider-neutral LLM client wrapper that returns null/no-op when unconfigured, so Phase 5 features fail gracefully.
prep.understand: No LLM SDK exists in this codebase. This one task unblocks everything in Phase 5. MiniMax (api.minimax.io) is Haniel's house model — it's OpenAI API-compatible, so the `openai` npm package + a `OPENAI_BASE_URL` env var override is the cleanest integration path. The fallback is critical: `lib/advisor/insights.ts` (the deterministic 6-rule advisor) must keep working without any AI credentials. Brain has 0 unresolved contradictions — clean path.
approach: Run `pnpm add openai` in the project root.
Create `lib/ai/client.ts`: read `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_BASE_URL` from env; if both present, construct `new OpenAI({ apiKey, baseURL })`; if absent, return null.
Export a `chat(messages: { role: string; content: string }[]): Promise<string>` helper — calls the client's `chat.completions.create()` or returns `''` when client is null.
Add `OPENAI_API_KEY=` and `OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://api.minimax.io/v1` to `.env.example` (blank key so nothing leaks).
Run `tsc --noEmit` to confirm zero type errors.
resources: api.minimax.io docs (MiniMax OpenAI-compatible API — confirm /v1/chat/completions endpoint)
npm: openai (npm.im/openai — use the installed version compatible with the project's Node)
lib/advisor/insights.ts (deterministic advisor — the Phase 5 fallback target, see the Insight[] shape)

tasks.title: Household Cash Flow engine — safe-to-spend + available-to-invest
tasks.notes: REMAINING: monthlyInvestmentsCents is hardcoded 0 in dashboard page.tsx (~L301-309) — wire it to RecurringContribution schedules so safe-to-spend stops overstating by the auto-invest reserve.

prep.what: Fix the hardcoded `monthlyInvestmentsCents = 0` bug in the dashboard — query RecurringContribution totals and thread them into the safe-to-spend formula.
prep.understand: Safe-to-spend = income − fixed bills − investing − discretionary. The 'investing' term is currently 0 — the app ignores your recurring investment contributions when calculating spendable cash, so the number overstates by whatever you auto-invest monthly. The `RecurringContribution` Prisma model already stores these schedules; the fix queries it and passes the monthly total into the existing formula. Owner-scoping should mirror the pattern in `lib/finance/net-worth.ts`. Brain is clean — 0 unresolved contradictions.
approach: Find the hardcoded value at `app/(app)/dashboard/page.tsx` ~L301-309 — confirm the exact variable name and what data shape the safe-to-spend function expects.
Check `lib/finance/bill-costs.ts` (or `lib/finance/cash-flow.ts`) to see if RecurringContribution is already queried anywhere — reuse rather than duplicate.

Add or extend a data-fetching function: `prisma.recurringContribution.aggregate({ where: { active: true, ownerUserId: ... }, _sum: { amountCents: true } })` — owner-scope it the same way net-worth.ts does.
Thread the result as `monthlyInvestmentsCents` into the safe-to-spend dashboard call.
Verify: the dashboard card shows a lower (more accurate) safe-to-spend number. Run `tsc --noEmit` + unit tests.
resources: prisma/schema.prisma (RecurringContribution model — check field names: amountCents, active, ownerUserId)
lib/finance/bill-costs.ts (existing recurring query pattern to reuse)
